Without the suppression the route could never record the durable failure for a cancelled operation at all — the awaited coroutine's own outcome is unaffected either way. Two things bound what is actually suppressed: (a) we are already unwinding a cancellation, so there is no successful outcome to corrupt; and (b) the durable record is written by the shielded call itself, which runs under its own transaction — its failure would be a DB-level fault whose evidence is the operation row staying in its prior state, and the guided-operation reconciliation path treats an unsettled lease as expired and takes it over. Raising here would replace a cancellation with a spurious 500 and lose the 499 conversion three lines below.
